newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade slow at $63 -feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade slow at $63 -feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle near midday Thursday traded in light volume at $63.00 per cwt, unchanged from this week's sales, feedlot sources said.
They said about 700 steers and heifers likely to grade select and choice sold in the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area and about 100 heifers sold in Kansas Thursday morning.
Week-to-date movement was estimated near 88,500 head in the Panhandle area and near 80,000 in Kansas, sources said.
Demand for cattle was winding down following two weeks of active buying by packers who now could be faced with an inventory surplus if beef buying slows, market sources noted.
The prospect of reduced retail beef demand reportedly had several packers seeking extensions beyond normal seven-day pickup dates for cattle bought last week, market sources said.
The recent skid in wholesale beef prices has resulted in active retail buying the past few weeks but that buying was expected to slow as retail coolers are filled, sources said.

Beef prices at midday were quoted down $0.19 to $0.48 per cwt, with 250 fabricated loads sold, USDA said. Heavyweight choice beef was quoted at $98.24, down $0.29 from Wednesday, but down $2.66 since Friday and down $6.40 from $104.64 from the closing quote three weeks ago, USDA statistics showed.
